_comment: Per-recipe tolerance for the closed-form physics pre-check (ticket 09).
Data, not code: what counts as a disagreement worth raising is a domain
judgement about how good the closed form is for that structure, and it
belongs where the domain knowledge lives. `tolerance_pct` is the signed
disagreement between the estimator's prediction and the spec's stated
target beyond which the Clarification block surfaces both numbers for the
user to arbitrate. The check NEVER blocks and never overrides the user.
A spec's own `target.tolerance_pct` wins when it is present; these are the
fallback and the record of how far each closed form can be trusted.

inset-fed-rectangular-patch.note: Balanis 14-1/14-2/14-7 are good to a few percent on a thin substrate; FR4's own permittivity tolerance dominates the error.

bow-tie-patch.note: Wider than the patch: a bow-tie's resonance is not set by a single closed-form length. Validated against the delivered pilot model, where the equilateral-triangle relation predicts within ~1% of the measured 3.85 GHz.

microstrip-line.note: Hammerstad-Jensen is quoted at ~1% for W/h in 0.1-10; 3% leaves room for the substrate's own tolerance.

parallel-coupled-line-filter.note: v1 checks the feed-line synthesis only. The coupled-section design is not estimated, so a PASS here says less than it does for the other recipes.

pyramidal-horn.note: v1 checks the feed waveguide's TE10 cutoff against the operating band, not the aperture gain. Wide, because it is a sanity check rather than a prediction.
